From b1e125ae425aba9b45252e933ca8df52a843ec70 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Victor Nogueira <victor@mojatatu.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 16:01:24 -0300
Subject: [PATCH] net/sched: ets: Remove drr class from the active list if it
 changes to strict

Whenever a user issues an ets qdisc change command, transforming a
drr class into a strict one, the ets code isn't checking whether that
class was in the active list and removing it. This means that, if a
user changes a strict class (which was in the active list) back to a drr
one, that class will be added twice to the active list [1].

Doing so with the following commands:

tc qdisc add dev lo root handle 1: ets bands 2 strict 1
tc qdisc add dev lo parent 1:2 handle 20: \
    tbf rate 8bit burst 100b latency 1s
tc filter add dev lo parent 1: basic classid 1:2
ping -c1 -W0.01 -s 56 127.0.0.1
tc qdisc change dev lo root handle 1: ets bands 2 strict 2
tc qdisc change dev lo root handle 1: ets bands 2 strict 1
ping -c1 -W0.01 -s 56 127.0.0.1

Will trigger the following splat with list debug turned on:

[   59.279014][  T365] 
diff --git a/net/sched/sch_ets.c b/net/sched/sch_ets.c
index ae46643e596d..306e046276d4 100644
--- a/net/sched/sch_ets.c
+++ b/net/sched/sch_ets.c
@@ -664,6 +664,10 @@ static int ets_qdisc_change(struct Qdisc *sch, struct nlattr *opt,
 			q->classes[i].deficit = quanta[i];
 		}
 	}
+	for (i = q->nstrict; i < nstrict; i++) {
+		if (cl_is_active(&q->classes[i]))
+			list_del_init(&q->classes[i].alist);
+	}
 	WRITE_ONCE(q->nstrict, nstrict);
 	memcpy(q->prio2band, priomap, sizeof(priomap));
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies `net/sched/sch_ets.c` to fix a bug where transitioning a class from DRR to strict during an ETS qdisc change fails to remove it from the active list.

**Modification**:  
In the `ets_qdisc_change` function, after quanta values are updated for strict classes, a new loop is added (lines 664-668). For each class whose band index falls between the old `q->nstrict` and the new `nstrict`, if the class is active (`cl_is_active`), it is removed from the active list via `list_del_init(&q->classes[i].alist)`.

**Relationship**:  
The single-file change directly addresses the root cause: when a DRR class becomes strict, it must no longer be in the active list (used for DRR scheduling). Without this removal, a later reversion to DRR would add the class a second time, causing list corruption. The fix ensures correct active list management during class type transitions.
